summary:
Our game is a survival and exploration adventure set in Valles Marineris on Mars. You play as an astronaut living at a research base and remotely controlling a rover. Your goal is to complete eight scientific missions before your oxygen runs out. You start with 20 minutes real time oxygen, limited food supplies, and a rover.
The base includes a control room, crew quarters, and a hydroponics room. From the computer, you can operate the rover to explore research sites, collect virtual rock samples, and investigate geological features. The missions introduce ancient water, landslides, seasonal dark streaks, rock layers, fractures, and the challenges of planning a safe rover route. Completing all eight missions triggers your rescue and return home.
To survive, you must manage food, water, and the rover’s battery. The rover can collect ice from an underground source and deliver it to the base where it will be melted into water. You then use that water to drink, care for plants which are located on the base and replenish food supplies. During exploration, temperature, sandstorms, and solar flares affect the rover. You can adjust its power, stop during daylight to recharge, and switch off its systems to protect it from solar flares.
The game is designed for children aged 7–12, encouraging curiosity about planetary science, geology, and space exploration. Its simplified mechanics draw on NASA information about Martian days and temperatures.
details:
Our game is a survival and exploration adventure set in Valles Marineris on Mars. You play as an astronaut living at a research base and remotely controlling a rover. Your goal is to complete eight scientific missions before your oxygen runs out. You start with 20 minutes real time oxygen, limited food supplies, and a rover.

The base includes a control room, crew quarters, and a hydroponics room. From the computer, you can operate the rover to explore research sites, collect virtual rock samples, and investigate geological features. The missions introduce ancient water, landslides, seasonal dark streaks, rock layers, fractures, and the challenges of planning a safe rover route. Completing all eight missions triggers your rescue and return home.

To survive, you must manage food, water, and the rover’s battery. The rover can collect ice from an underground source and deliver it to the base where it will be melted into water. You then use that water to drink, care for plants which are located on the base and replenish food supplies. During exploration, temperature, sandstorms, and solar flares affect the rover. You can adjust its power, stop during daylight to recharge, and switch off its systems to protect it from solar flares. At the base, sleeping in the crew quarters lets you skip the night, but still consumes oxygen and food.

The game is designed for children aged 7–12, encouraging curiosity about planetary science, geology, and space exploration. Its simplified mechanics draw on NASA information about Martian days and temperatures. Scientific uncertainty is part of the experience: evidence of ancient water does not prove that liquid water is flowing on Mars today.



Programming language used to create game: Python 3.13 with module Pygame. The project is developed in Visual studio code
